 Daniel Radcliffe politely noncommittal about watching Harry Potter series
 "Eight hours is a lot of anything to watch," he said. 
 Olivia Singh --> 
 By Olivia Singh  |  
 November 9, 2026 | 3:47pm 
 Photo: Noam Galai/Getty Images for Netflix

 Daniel Radcliffe isn’t sure he’ll end up watching HBO’s Harry Potter reboot—not necessarily because he’s strongly against the project (as many are ), but because he’s already spent enough time at Hogwarts and isn’t much of a TV watcher anyway. “I don’t know if I will [watch], honestly,” Radcliffe told the Associated Press at the premiere of his new animated film, Steps , on Sunday. “I’ve been in a lot of Harry Potter already. And also, I don’t watch any TV. I haven’t seen Breaking Bad . I haven’t seen Mad Men . I haven’t seen some of the real classics. So, eight hours is a lot of anything to watch.” It’s understandable that Radcliffe might not tune in when the series premieres its first season on December 25. (A second season has already been confirmed, and HBO ultimately hopes to adapt all seven of J.K. Rowling’s books.) He’s already been there, done that, having starred alongside Rupert Grint and Emma Watson in eight films released between 2001 and 2011. Even many fans who grew up with the franchise don’t see the point of revisiting the story, especially given J.K. Rowling’s persistent anti-trans views and her involvement as an executive producer . (Radcliffe has distanced himself from these views multiple times .) 
 The ever-polite Radcliffe has previously commented on the reboot, supporting the young actors taking over the franchise. Having gone through the wringer himself as a child star, Radcliffe has been fiercely protective of Dominic McLaughlin, who’s playing the titular wizard, and the rest of the cast. During an appearance on Good Morning America last year, Radcliffe revealed that he wrote a letter to McLaughlin offering his support and best wishes. “I just see these pictures of him and the other kids and I just want to hug them,” he said. “They just seem so young. I just look at them and say, ‘Oh, it’s crazy I was doing that at that age.’ But it’s also incredibly sweet and I hope they’re having a great time.” Then, in a February interview with ScreenRant , Radcliffe urged fans not to constantly ask the young actors about him, Grint, and Watson. “I would like not to be weird spectral phantoms in these children’s lives,” he said. Speaking to the Associated Press, Radcliffe reiterated that he doesn’t feel a need to offer McLaughlin any advice, at least not publicly. “I don’t want to haunt this poor child through interviews,” he said. “So I have no advice for him. He’s going to be amazing, and I think I will get to meet him someday—and I’m very excited about that.”
